title: Three-sweep reset run
statement: Let $S$ be a deterministic Boolean-tape Turing machine and $A$ a nondeterministic Boolean-tape Turing machine, with a Boolean loop parameter and input word $x$. For any natural number $m$, input-head position, and simulated-machine tape contents and head positions, if a choice word $w$ has length $3(m+1)$, then running the host machine under $w$ from phase $p0$ with yard head at $m-1$ ends in the running phase with $A$ in its initial state and no captured output; the input head is moved left by $m+1$ positions with boundary clamping and then one position right, every head of $A$’s work tapes advances by $3(m+1)$, the yard head is at $0$, and the other tapes and output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Arbitrary simulated-machine tape contents and head positions
